title: Interpretations of the derivative
goal: Turn derivative numbers into plain-English sentences about real-world speed, growth, cost, or temperature—complete with the right units.

beforeThis.skill: Quick check: the units of a derivative $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ are always "(units of output $y$) per (unit of input $x$)"—for example, $\text{grams per hour}$ or $\text{dollars per item}$.

questions.asking: Explain in physical terms (including units of metres per hour) what the 24-hour secant slope and the $t = 0$ tangent slope represent for the water height at the dam.
questions.statement:
Suppose $h(t)$ gives the height at time $t$ of the water at a dam, where the units of $t$ are hours and the units of $h$ are meters.

  1. What is the physical interpretation of the slope of the secant line through the points $(0, h(0))$ and $(24, h(24))$?
  2. What is the physical interpretation of the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y = h(t)$ at the point $(0, h(0))$?

questions.asking: Describe in practical terms what $p'(t)$ measures when $p(t)$ is the profit from selling $t$ widgets.
questions.statement: Suppose $p(t)$ is a function that gives the profit generated by selling $t$ widgets. What is the practical interpretation of $p'(t)$?

questions.asking: State the physical meaning of $T'(d)$ in degrees per metre of depth, and reason whether water temperature changes more rapidly near the surface or deep underwater.
questions.statement: $T(d)$ gives the temperature of water at a particular location $d$ metres below the surface. What is the physical interpretation of $T'(d)$? Would you expect the magnitude of $T'(d)$ to be larger when $d$ is near $0$, or when $d$ is very large?

questions.asking: Explain in one plain-English sentence what $C'(w)$ means: how many extra calories come from adding $1$ more gram of weight $w$.
questions.statement: $C(w)$ gives the calories in $w$ grams of a particular dish. What does $C'(w)$ describe?

questions.asking: Name the physical quantity represented by the rate of change of velocity $v'(t)$ with respect to time.
questions.statement: The velocity of a moving object at time $t$ is given by $v(t)$. What is $v'(t)$?

questions.asking: Explain in plain English what $T'(j)$ means: how many degrees Celsius the temperature rises per $1$ joule of heat added.
questions.statement: The function $T(j)$ gives the temperature in degrees Celsius of a cup of water after $j$ joules of heat have been added. What is $T'(j)$?

questions.asking: Describe what $P'(T)$ means for how the final bacteria count responds to a small change in incubation temperature $T$.
questions.statement: A population of bacteria, left for a fixed amount of time at temperature $T$, grows to $P(T)$ individuals. Interpret $P'(T)$.

questions.asking: Write a formula in terms of $R'(t)$ that converts the rotational speed from rotations per second into degrees per second.
questions.statement: You hammer a small nail into a wooden wagon wheel. $R(t)$ gives the number of rotations the nail has undergone $t$ seconds after the wagon started to roll. Give an equation for how quickly the nail is rotating, measured in degrees per second.

questions.asking: Explain how the sign of $P'(T)$ tells you whether the current temperature $T$ is below or above the ideal growth temperature.
questions.statement: A population of bacteria, left for a fixed amount of time at temperature $T$, grows to $P(T)$ individuals. There is one ideal temperature where the bacteria population grows largest, and the closer the sample is to that temperature, the larger the population is (unless the temperature is so extreme that it causes all the bacteria to die by freezing or boiling). How will $P'(T)$ tell you whether you are colder or hotter than the ideal temperature?
